messages:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: node-pool-gpu-us-west local-nvme iops drop (>60% below baseline) detected for 12m. impacted pods: gpu-serving-*. Suggest investigating ephemeral cleaner activity. link: https://grafana.internal/r/ABCD1234
ana: seeing failed GPU provision attempts in the last 15m, kube events show image pulls stuck on nodes with high disk wait. cc @infra-oncall
leo: can someone run iostat + nvme smart while we correlate? guessing write latency + queue depth spike.
maya: pulled logs from node-3: "nvme0n1: I/O 3072 queued, completion latency 25ms, read_err_count 3" 
ana: also noticed ephemeral-cleaner logs spiking: "sweep_batch=4096 concurrency=8 duration=14m" -- looks like GC is backing up and hammering IOPS.
sam: if cleaner is scanning huge numbers of small files we get metadata ops thrash. temp mitigation: reduce cleaner concurrency and pivot to time-windowed deletes.
leo: +1. try `kubectl -n infra logs ephemeral-cleaner-*.` and run: ```ssh node-3 sudo iostat -x 1 5 && sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1```
infra-oncall: running iostat now, will paste results. also increasing cleaner backoff to 30s and concurrency->2 on the affected pool.
monitoring-bot: CONFIG CHANGE DETECTED: ephemeral-cleaner concurrency set to 2 for node-pool-gpu-us-west by infra-oncall at 1954321050
ana: after backoff change, I see write_iops drop from 18k -> 6k and queue depth stabilize. provisioning retries still failing due to kubelet ImagePull backoffs on 3 nodes.
leo: image pulls hit the same disk path? could be overlayfs metadata pressure. check `df -i` and containerd status.
maya: df -i on node-3 shows inode usage 98% on /var/lib/containerd. lots of tiny layers from local build artifacts.
sam: two options: 1) evict non-critical pods on those nodes and run an aggressive docker GC (risky during traffic) 2) cordon+reboot nodes (fast) 3) replace NVMe if SMART shows wear. cost/tradeoffs?
infra-oncall: proposing cordon + drain low-priority GPU nodes, run aggressive file GC (containerd prune, tmp cleanup), and then uncordon after verification. schedule in 10m window.
leo: add a small temporary admission controller tweak to route new GPU provisioning to other region (us-east) while we remediate. reduces customer impact.
ana: can we also enable prefix/KV caching for the heaviest serving routes to reduce subsequent writes? that might reduce churn but is longer-term.
sam: created quick runbook gist: https://git.internal/runs/cleanup-cordon-195432 -- includes exact commands: ```kubectl cordon node-3 && kubectl drain node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60``` and containerd prune commands. use with caution.
infra-oncall: starting cordon/drain run on node-3, node-4, node-7. will post status. ETA 12m.
maya: copying relevant SMART output: `percentage_used=42, media_errors=0, critical_warning=0, temp=38C` so wear not urgent. prefer software GC first.
monitoring-bot: NOTE: provisioning error rate decreased by 40% after cordon/drain started (metric: kube.provision.errors).
ana: nice. follow-up action: add inode pressure alert to monitoring (threshold 90%) and add ephemeral-cleaner guardrails to avoid full-scans when inode pressure >85%.
leo: also add a short-term quota on local build artifacts on CI runners hitting those pools.
infra-oncall: agreed. I'll open a ticket and schedule an infra postmortem doc with timeline and decisions. rolling reboots avoided: no replacement NVMe required at this time.
sam: marking follow-ups: monitor inode alert, cleaner guardrails, route-protection for GPU provisioning, and CI quotas. assigned to infra team. :memo:
infra-oncall: all drains completed, nodes back in service, provisioning retries succeeded. closing the incident thread. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
